brief: A single hex base, nothing else added beside or on top of it, with five drawers in it.

requirements.evidence: piece:0,0,0;full is the only part, as before. I changed nothing.

requirements.requirement: Nothing else added beside or on top of it
requirements.evidence: I added nothing. The build is still the one base.

find_sockets for drawers returned no offers on the full base. Drawers only go on the cut face of a half base, one per face, so one base can't take five. Notch drawers and bays would need neighbouring bases, which the brief rules out.

finish.summary: I didn't build this, because one hex base can't hold five drawers. The configurator offers no drawer sockets on the full base that's there now. Drawers only sit on the flat cut face of a half base, so a single half base gives you room for one drawer front, not five. The other drawer types (notch drawers and bays) need two or three bases touching, which would break your "nothing beside it" rule. I left the build as it was: one full base, unchanged. Here's what I could build instead: (a) one half base with a single drawer (it can be one, two or three storeys tall), (b) a small group of half bases, one drawer each, to reach five, or (c) one full base with bins inside it instead of drawers.
